sql: SELECT sum(c) OVER (ORDER BY a GROUPS BETWEEN . PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING)
why: DuckDB accepts a lone dot as the first bound of GROUPS BETWEEN (not of ROWS or RANGE BETWEEN, nor as the second bound); the parser rejects it

sql: SELECT sum(b) OVER (ORDER BY a ROWS BETWEEN NOT 1 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING)
why: DuckDB rejects NOT at the start of the first bound after BETWEEN (not after ROWS, nor as the second bound); the parser accepts it
DuckDB rejects SETOF before a qualified type name; the parser accepts it
DuckDB accepts the percent sign after a postfix operator (-1| %); the parser rejects it, as it does after + and the other operators that bind more loosely than %

sql: SELECT sum(v) OVER (ORDER BY i RANGE BETWEEN IN PRECEDING AND -1 PRECEDING)
why: DuckDB accepts the word IN as the first bound of a frame before PRECEDING (and AND, and a dot after GROUPS BETWEEN); it is not understood why, and the parser rejects it

sql: SELECT sum(v) OVER (ORDER BY i RANGE BETWEEN AND PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING)

why: the pass that replaces Unicode white space (see above) makes DuckDB see an unterminated dollar-quoted string where the scanner finds the end of one

the same pass that replaces Unicode white space: it takes the dollar after the name for the start of a dollar-quoted string, leaves the space (U+2002) alone, and the scanner then reads it as part of an identifier
